mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increase and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and corporate earnings decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increase and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are revised downwards.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of periods with declining GDP, or the correlation between GDP growth and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth prospects improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increase and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.3% in a month, coupled with an increase in nonfarm payrolls by more than 200,000, signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer confidence and spending improve.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month AND PAYEMS increases > 200,000
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in housing starts by more than 10% in a month, combined with a decrease in the federal funds rate, signals a boost in demand and easing monetary conditions, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as construction and related industries benefit.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 10% in 1 month AND FEDFUNDS decreases
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of HOUST and FEDFUNDS on SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index by more than 0.5% per month for two consecutive months signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real returns are eroded and the Fed is expected to tighten monetary policy.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between CPIAUCSL increase and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in retail and food services sales by more than 1% in a month signals weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are revised downwards.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between RSAFS decrease and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
